learning_outcomes.text: Creates a block diagram for machine tools.
Performs computer numerical control of systems and machines.
Writes programs manually and reads existing programs.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course, explanation of its operation. Receiving student suggestions and expectations. Historical development of machine tools and CNC machines.
The most important components of manufacturing, numerically controlling and programming machine tools with the help of computers. CNC (Computer Numerical Control) Machine Tools.

Manufacturing process and its basic components, shaping elements, tools, shaped elements, parts, tools, parts and auxiliary systems ensuring coordination, machine and applied process, manufacturing method

Manufacturing-Machining Quality (tolerance) Concept; Dimensional Tolerances, Form Tolerances, Surface Tolerances, Factors affecting machining quality; machine-dependent, tool system-dependent, part system-dependent, environment-dependent, control system-dependent etc.

Classification of machine tools, according to manufacturing method, according to manufacturing quantity and speed, according to control system; manual control, automatic control; mechanical automatons, numerical automatons, computer numerical controlled machines; identification, classification, co
Computer numerical controlled machines; construction principles, tool system, part system, drive systems, motors, sensors, control system.
CNC programming methods; manual program writing, dialogue method, program creation from drawing, reverse engineering
ISO programming method and G codes, Turning and Program Creation
ISO programming method and G codes, Milling and Program Creation
ISO programming method and G codes, Machining Center and Program Creation
ISO programming method and G codes, Wire EDM and Program Creation
Application; CNC Wire EDM Machine, Program Creation, Transfer to Machine and Machining
Application; CNC Machining Center, Program Creation, Transfer to Machine and Machining
Application; Turning, Program Creation, Transfer to Machine and Machining
Student Presentations, general evaluation of the course.
assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated by weighting in-term success at 60% and the final exam at 40%. In-term success is composed of a midterm exam (40%), four quizzes (5% each), one assignment (10%), one laboratory performance task (15%), and one workshop performance task (15%).
